target: route "howard-cube" (hcube): bottom-antipodal walks on LP orientations of cubes — Klee–Minty, Amenta–Ziegler deformed products, Holt–Klee, and one-player realisability

findings.defect: GAP (asserted, not proved): the induction consumes, without proof, that the deformed product P_1 ⋉ … ⋉ P_{k−1} of the first k−1 factors again satisfies the standing hypothesis of def:hcube-deformed — that it is a polytope whose face lattice is that of P_1 × … × P_{k−1} — equivalently, that the m_k block-k constraints not tight at w*_k are redundant on the face G = {w_k = w*_k}.
findings.evidence: The proof says only 'π carries the vertices of G bijectively onto the vertices of P_1 ⋉ … ⋉ P_{k−1}, which are computed by the same recursion from the same constraints; two polytopes with the same vertex set are equal'. 'Two polytopes with the same vertex set are equal' presupposes that P_{<k} is bounded and has exactly those vertices — which is the induction hypothesis, not something established. The block-1 case is trivial (D_1 is empty) but k ≥ 3 is not. The gap is repairable in two lines and I checked the repair: G is full-dimensional in the y_{<k} coordinates and, by the product face lattice, each of its Σ_{i<k} 2m_i facets is cut by a block-i constraint, so G equals the intersection of those halfspaces and the extra block-k constraints are redundant. Everything else in the proof reconstructs: the fibre-rigidity argument (same normal fan, edge direction spanning ker{C_r : r∈T}, sign fixed by C_{j_0}) is correct, and the autonomy/confinement step is correct. Numerically I rebuilt the theorem from its statement on my own instances (/tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-howard-cube-correctness/dprod.py, runcert.py): 950+ deformed products of k=2,3 quadrilaterals, each FULLY certified in exact rationals (all 4^k transversals feasible with exactly 2k tight, every one of the other C(4k,2k) bases singular or infeasible, recession cone with no extreme ray) — 0 violations of fibre rigidity, 0 of last-block autonomy, 0 of h_BA ≤ d; plus 429 certified deformed cubes in d=3..7 with the last coordinate uniform in every one. (Caution recorded for the record: a weaker certification that only checks the transversals admits non-polytopes, on which the 'orientation' can even be cyclic; the fully certified run above is the one that counts.)

findings.defect: GAP (asserted, not verified): the statement 'there are one-player stopping SSGs … whose all-switches runs have length 9 at m=5 and 12 at m=6' is supported only by harmonic normal forms; the average part that realises the dyadic rows — the binary-expansion chain that the project's standing note attached to lem:gadget/sec:fold says 'a route that needs it must implement and verify it itself' — is never exhibited, and no vertex count is given (contrast prop:no-linear-tiebreak in frontier.tex, which does give '34 vertices, 28 of them average').
findings.evidence: I closed the gap myself rather than merely flagging it. /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-howard-cube-correctness/realise.py builds a fair-coin SSG from each printed normal form by a memoised binary tree of depth 12 over 4096 leaves (identical subtrees shared), carrying the sinks as sentinels and mapping them to indices only at the end. m=5: N = 327 (5 Max, 320 average, 2 sinks); m=6: N = 319 (6 Max, 311 average, 2 sinks). For every one of the 10 (resp. 12) actions the gadget's first-passage law onto (x_1..x_m, t_1), computed structurally by DAG back-substitution, equals the printed row exactly over D = 4096. The greatest trap of the m=5 game is EMPTY (lem:trapchar ⇒ stopping), every non-sink has out-degree 2, and no vertex index collides with the sinks (audit_m5_game.json). Recomputing the all-switches run FROM THE GAME (exact rationals, strict switchable set): ties = 0, improvement orientation is a USO, acyclic and Holt–Klee, max BA height 9 at m=5 and 12 at m=6. So the claim is TRUE and h*_1(5) ≥ 9, h*_1(6) ≥ 12 stand; only the verification was missing from the route.

findings.defect: Internal inconsistency of convention: thm:hcube-dprod's proof fixes the sink as the MINIMISER of c ('on each face the objective attains its minimum at a unique vertex, which is the face's unique sink, and the objective strictly decreases along the orientation'), whereas prop:hcube-km's outmap formula and its 'sink (0,…,0,1)' for the Klee–Minty cube with objective x_d, and prop:hcube-lp4(iii) ('v ∈ s(σ) exactly when c·x_{σ⊕e_v} > c·x_σ'), fix the sink as the MAXIMISER. The sentence 'the bound of thm:hcube-dprod is attained' therefore compares two oppositely oriented objects as written. This inconsistency is now in frontier.tex (proof of thm:deformed-flat vs prop:km-measured).
findings.evidence: For the Klee–Minty cube with objective x_d the vertex b = (0,…,0,1) has x_d = 1, the maximum, so 'sink (0,…,0,1)' is the max convention; the min-convention sink is b = 0 (I computed both in /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-howard-cube-correctness/km.py: sinks 2^{d−1} vs 0 for d = 2..10). Under the min convention the stated outmap s(b) = {i : b_i ≡ b_{i+1}+…+b_d} is the complement of the truth. No numerical claim is damaged — I verified BA height = d and longest monotone path = 2^d − 1 under BOTH conventions for d = 2..10, and h*_LP is convention-free because −c is admissible whenever c is — but the statements as written are mutually inconsistent and should be reconciled before integration.

findings.defect: A sentence in the proof is false: 'the source-sink pair of G is that of F translated by e_i, and the two pairs are disjoint exactly when the source and sink of F are adjacent along j'. The two pairs are ALSO disjoint when src F and snk F are antipodal in the square.
findings.evidence: In a 2-face with coordinates (i,j): if {src,snk} = {a, a⊕e_i⊕e_j} then its e_i-translate is {a⊕e_i, a⊕e_j}, disjoint from it. The sentence is not load-bearing — in the antipodal case F has no source–sink EDGE, so condition (T) holds there anyway, and the correct biconditional is '(T) fails on the face {i,j} iff src F and snk F are adjacent along j', which is what the rest of the argument uses. The corollary's conclusion is correct: I verified 'if (T) holds on every 2-face containing i then coordinate i is uniform in s' over all 4 + 54 + 50560 = 50618 (seed, coordinate) pairs at dimensions 2, 3, 4 (my own 12640-class census), 11329+27+4 of which satisfy (T), with 0 violations; and 'no outer coordinate of a blow-up is ever uniform' over 308 outer coordinates, 0 uniform.

findings.defect: The 'if' direction concludes that P is 'a polytope combinatorially equivalent to the m-cube' from 'simple, 2m facets in m opposite pairs, graph the m-cube', which needs either Blind–Mani–Kalai (uncited) or the two-line face-lattice argument the proof omits.
findings.evidence: Repair: by (i) each x_σ has exactly the m transversal constraints tight, so the face cut by facet (v,a) is conv{x_σ : σ(v) = a}; opposite facets share no vertex, hence (a face being the hull of the vertices it contains) are disjoint; so faces of P correspond bijectively to partial transversals, i.e. to faces of the cube. The certificate itself verifies exactly as claimed: I re-checked the printed A, b, c (denominator 64) in exact rationals — all 16 transversals feasible with exactly 4 tight, all 54 non-transversal bases infeasible (none singular), no extreme ray of the recession cone, 0 tied edges, induced orientation exactly (5,8,10,11,9,12,14,15,13,4,6,7,2,3,1,0), USO, acyclic, Holt–Klee, BA height 6.

findings.defect: The headline 'BA height at most the sum of its factors' heights' is stronger than what is proved. The proved bound is Σ_i h*_LP(m_i) — the sum of the CEILINGS — because the induction replaces the objective on the lower blocks (c_{<k}·y_{<k} + c_k·y_k(y_{<k})), so nothing in the argument controls the lower factors' own induced orientations σ_1,…,σ_{k−1}.
findings.evidence: The two agree for deformed cubes (h*_LP(1) = 1 = h(σ_i) always) but not for quadrilateral factors, where h(σ_i) may be 1 while h*_LP(2) = 2. The LaTeX (thm:hcube-dprod and the integrated thm:deformed-flat) states the correct form Σ_i h*_LP(m_i); only the JSON headline overstates.

findings.defect: The headline claim 'closes the classical geometric arsenal as a source for the pivot' holds only for deformed products whose factors are combinatorially cubes of BOUNDED dimension; the theorem's hypothesis requires every factor to be combinatorially a cube (so genuine Amenta–Ziegler products of general polygons are outside it), and for factors of growing dimension Σ_i h*_LP(m_i) is not sub-linear in any useful sense (two 3-cube factors already give the bound 8 at d = 6).
findings.evidence: rem:hcube-km and the integrated text state the hedged version correctly ('no family of deformed products with factors of bounded dimension has superlinear bottom-antipodal height'), so this is a headline-only overreach.

findings.defect: The fourth row of the table is not an independent datum: by the route's own argument a nonsingular diagonal rescaling of the variables leaves the objective values at vertices unchanged, so the 'Goldfarb–Sit rescaling' row is literally the Klee–Minty row. Presenting it as a fourth family in a four-row table adds nothing.
findings.evidence: The route discloses this in its own 'argument' field, and the version already integrated into frontier.tex as prop:km-measured has dropped the row. I independently reproduced the two rows that carry content: Klee–Minty with ε ∈ {1/4, 1/10} for d = 2..12 and Chvátal's form for d = 2..10, in exact rationals — no ties, USO, acyclic, longest directed path exactly 2^d − 1, BA height exactly d, and the outmap identity s(b) = {i : b_i ≡ b_{i+1}+…+b_d (mod 2)} exact for every b and every d in range.

findings.defect: The report's verification field says the program 'reproduces the paper's fact that exactly four of the eight height-2 seeds of the 2-cube give a Holt–Klee B'. That is inaccurate as phrased: every one of the eight height-2 USOs of the 2-cube has TWO vertices of maximal height, and for exactly one of the two choices of u (the one making z = o ⊕ u a single coordinate) the blow-up is Holt–Klee. So all eight seeds give a Holt–Klee B, and the correct count is 8 of the 16 (seed, u) pairs.
findings.evidence: Exhaustive check over the 8 height-2 USOs of the 2-cube: for each, one choice of u gives a Holt–Klee B of height 6 and the other (z = 1̄) does not. rem:blowup-measured in frontier.tex states this correctly; the error is only in the route's report text, not in its LaTeX.

verdict:
Nothing fatal or major survived. I rebuilt every numerical and computational claim from the STATEMENT, with my own code, in exact rational arithmetic, in /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-howard-cube-correctness/ (acube.py, trace5.c, complete.c, census4.c, km.py, blow.py, dprod.py, oneplayer.py, realise.py). EVERY claim reproduced, several of them exactly to the digit.

REPRODUCED. (1) Library validation: my USO/AUSO/Holt–Klee code reproduces prop:auso-census independently — 12/744 USOs at m=2,3 with 728 acyclic in 18 classes, 656 HK in 16 classes, h*(3)=4, h*_HK(3)=4; and my own C census of the 4-cube gives 346359 USOs with sink at 0 (×16 = 5541744), 299511 acyclic (×16 = 4792176), 12640 classes, heights 1:1, 2:754, 3:4776, 4:5404, 5:1561, 6:143 (56 HK), 7:1 (0 HK), 6113 HK classes. On G#'s outmap my max-flow test returns 2 paths where 4 are needed and names the failing 3-face {x1,x2,x4} at x3=1, exactly as cor:seven-two-player says, and the heights match prop:auso-seven's printed vector. (2) hcube:hkfive: my independent trace enumerator reproduces prop:hstar-five's whole table including 347640 traces at length 12 and 22320 at length 13; my independent completion search gives L=13 → 0 completions, L=12 with NO Holt–Klee prune → 480 acyclic USO completions of which 0 are Holt–Klee (a strictly stronger statement than the route's pruned 0), L=12 with the prune → 0, L=11 with the prune → 3120 survivors whose lex-first is the route's witness verbatim; the witness re-verifies as a bijection, USO on all 496 pairs, acyclic, height vector exactly as printed, max 11, Holt–Klee on all 51 faces of dimension ≥ 3. h*_HK(5) = 11 is confirmed. (The route's control figure '168 completions / 48 acyclic at m=4, L=7' reproduces exactly, but only when the acyclicity prune is also off — with it on the count is 48/48; not a defect, just an unstated variant.) (3) hcube:km: Klee–Minty (ε = 1/4, 1/10, d = 2..12) and Chvátal (d = 2..10) all give longest monotone path 2^d − 1 and BA height exactly d, no ties, with the stated outmap identity exact; Chvátal's l_i < u_i verified at every vertex. (4) hcube:stack: both rules confirmed as exact iff-statements, 168/192 and 16/144 failures, zero exceptions. (5) hcube:blowfaces: I implemented B(s,z) from thm:blowup's table (B of the 1-cube = [0,1,3,6,7,4,5,2], height 4, HK) and confirmed the structural identifications (i) and (ii) literally — 3488 3-face comparisons against the stacking construction, 0 mismatches — and that (P)∧(T) is NECESSARY for Holt–Klee over 154 blow-ups (all AUSO classes m ≤ 3, all z), 0 violations, with 3 instances where (P)∧(T) holds and HK fails (so 'necessary only' is right). B² = B(B(1-cube), z = 4) reproduces the outmap recorded in the project memory verbatim, height 10, not HK, with exactly six failing 3-faces, one (P) pair and two (T) pairs, as claimed. (6) hcube:parity: my census reproduces the route's parity-good table digit for digit — m=3: 14 of 18 classes, no height-4 class, max parity-good height 3; m=4: 1/1, 155/331 + 302/423, 989/2273 + 1489/2503, 1379/3003 + 1113/2401, 175/832 + 261/729, 16/87 + 15/56, 0/1. (7) hcube:transl: 50618 (seed, coordinate) pairs at dimensions 2, 3, 4 — exactly the route's count — 0 violations; outer coordinates never uniform. (8) hcube:blowbest: greatest Holt–Klee blow-up heights 4, 6, 8 at dimensions 3, 4, 5; twisted products 288 total / 186 non-HK / tallest HK = 5; 1-cube against the height-11 witness: the only Holt–Klee twist is the untwisted one, at height 11 (the height-12 twists are non-HK). (9) hcube:oneplayer: the printed m=5 and m=6 harmonic normal forms reproduce their outmaps, ties = 0, Holt–Klee, and runs 12,27,0,11,2,3,21,1,5,7 (length 9) and 25,14,33,6,37,46,45,44,16,56,24,28,12 (length 12) exactly; the repository games G_m3_k0_den64_s1 and AP_m4_k0_den256_s200 give heights 4 and 6 with 0 ties; and I built actual fair-coin SSGs (N = 327 and N = 319, greatest trap empty) realising the two normal forms and recomputed the runs from the games. (10) hcube:lp4: the printed dyadic certificate verifies exactly. (11) hcube:notdeformed and the table rem:hcube-table check out: h*_1 monotonicity is sound, and the AP_m4 orientation has in fact no uniform coordinate at all.

NOT CHECKED: I did not run or read the route's own code (deliberately); I did not reproduce its '210 deformed products' or '69 blow-up instances' counts (I ran my own 950+ and 154); I did not attempt to settle the five unresolved Holt–Klee classes at m=4 (I did verify all five are genuine Holt–Klee AUSO classes of the stated heights 5,5,4,4,3 and appear in my independent 12640-class census, and the route's 'gap' status with the disclosed non-discriminating control is honest); and I could not check the prior-art attributions (no web), which the route itself flags as from memory. No step of the route assumes a target-equivalent oracle, claims a decision rule, a barrier, or a polynomial class, so THE STANDING RULE and the equivalence traps do not bite; no val_σ is ever computed by greedy policy iteration (every value comes from an exact linear solve on a game with a strict per-row leak), rows are accumulated rather than written as dict literals, sinks are carried as sentinels, and the run lengths count productive rounds only.

One contextual note: frontier.tex has already been updated with this route's material (sec:deformed, def:deformed, lem:deformed-rigid, thm:deformed-flat, prop:km-measured, lem:stack, lem:blowup-faces, and prop:hkfive with the identical height-11 witness), so findings 1, 3, 5 and 6 above apply to text now standing in the paper.
